items.text: Bachelor's (BSc), Master's (MSc), and Doctoral (PhD) programs in English
Applications are submitted online; for example, for the 2025/26 academic year, applications are accepted between April 1 and May 31.
Detailed descriptions of the enrollment process and required documents can be found on the website of the Academic Services Centre (ASC/KTH).

With your admission letter, you receive a 6-character unique identifier (your Neptun code) and an initial password. Through Neptun, you can enroll for the semester, register for subjects, view your personal timetable, and sign up for exams.
Upload the necessary documents to Neptun as described in the enrollment newsletter. This will be followed by an in-person registration, where your documents will be checked.
Every student is automatically assigned a directory ID, which can be found on the directory administration page after logging in with your Neptun login credentials.
On the same admin page, you can also request access to Office 365 (O365), which gives you: University Wi-Fi, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive and other O365 services.

log in to the BME Directory Administration Page with your Neptun login details, select "Set up user account for Microsoft Office 365," choose your O365 username, tick "Yes" under "Request O365 access," and save.
Note: Microsoft has renamed O365 to M365, but most university pages still refer to it as O365.

You can find courses in two ways: by browsing based on language, department, and course name, or from the left-hand navigation menu, where only your own registered courses are listed — making them quick and easy to access.

groups.label: Getting to BME from the Airport

items.text: Bus 100E runs every 10 minutes from Liszt Ferenc Airport. Take the bus to Kálvin tér. From there, take metro line 4 towards Kelenföld, or trams 47 or 49 to the stop "Szent Gellért tér – Műegyetem." You can already see Building K from there.
For buses 100E and 200E, a special airport ticket is required, which can be bought on the buses, at the airport, or in the BudapestGO app. Download the BudapestGO app to conveniently buy a pass.

groups.label: Residence Permit
groups.text: To stay and study in Hungary you are required to obtain a residence permit. It can take quite a long time, so you should start as early as possible.

groups.label: TAJ Card / Private Health Insurance
groups.text: Scholarship holders (SH, SCYP, Diaspora) are entitled to free healthcare in Hungary once they have a TAJ card; fee-paying students can also obtain one, but only against a monthly contribution. Your TAJ number is also required to work legally in Hungary.

groups.label: Student ID Card
groups.text: Hungarian higher education students can get a free student ID card, which is required to prove your student status and is also needed to buy discounted public transport passes in Budapest.

groups.label: Hungarian Bank Account
groups.text: Opening a Hungarian bank account is needed for receiving scholarships, paying tuition, and other transfers.
